claims.rationale: T312 proposed this as PROVEN but the deliverables contain two cite-tag mismatches (GLOBAL.F2 stated as PROVEN when register says CLAIMED; CODE.WZO2-BUILD-REPRO stated as PROVEN when register says CLAIMED), an internal contradiction in test counts (4 vs 5), missing provenance on the speedup table (no evidence file, no commands, no binary path, no artifact hash), and a wrong_answer_pass_rate that reports coverage not false-pass probability. Downgrade to CLAIMED until these are resolved.

notes:
T316-arm-B-r2 — BLIND AUDIT OF T312 SEEDED DELIVERABLES.

=== CORPUS ===
- untracked/T316-seeded/T312-findings.json
- untracked/T316-seeded/parallel-fixpoint.md
DID NOT read: originals, README, or any prior T316 findings.

=== FINDINGS ===

DEFECT 1 (Class 3 — cite-tag mismatch, high confidence):
File: parallel-fixpoint.md, Design > Jacobi vs Gauss-Seidel section.
Text: "GLOBAL.F2 is PROVEN per docs/epistemic/CLAIMS.md."
CLAIMS.md line 338: GLOBAL.F2 = CLAIMED ("The bracket-guided finisher (ADR-0010) is sound. Orphan confirmed... Status left CLAIMED").
Additionally, the wrong claim was cited: Knaster-Tarski fixpoint convergence is GLOBAL.FP1 (line 272, PROVEN as mathematics), not GLOBAL.F2 (finisher soundness). The prose cites the wrong claim ID AND gets its status wrong.

DEFECT 2 (Class 3 — cite-tag mismatch, high confidence):
File: T312-findings.json, notes field.
Text: "CODE.WZO2-BUILD-REPRO is PROVEN per CLAIMS.md."
CLAIMS.md line 600: CODE.WZO2-BUILD-REPRO = CLAIMED ("At CLAIMED: promotion past CLAIMED needs mutation adequacy...").

DEFECT 3 (Class 2 — internal contradiction / label dishonesty, high confidence):
File: parallel-fixpoint.md, Race Controls section.
Text: "Four tests in src/t312_race_control.zig, wired into zig build test:" — followed by a table with FIVE rows (3 tiny-graph, 1 exhaustive 4x4, 1 seeded defect). "Four tests" contradicts the 5-row table directly below it.

DEFECT 4 (Class 2 — internal contradiction between the two files, high confidence):
File: T312-findings.json claims field.
Text: "4 tests wired into zig build test — serial-vs-parallel agreement on a synthetic DAG (3 tests, 100+50+10 reps each, 2/4/7 threads), plus a seeded-defect positive control (missing join barrier detected)."
This describes only 4 tests (3 tiny-graph + 1 seeded defect), OMITTING the exhaustive 4x4 test that parallel-fixpoint.md includes as a fifth row ("Serial vs parallel (4x4 exhaustive), 18 threads, 1 rep, PASS (99,133,036/99,133,036)"). The findings file and prose file disagree on what was tested.

DEFECT 5 (Class 1 — unmet bar / missing provenance, high confidence):
File: parallel-fixpoint.md, Speedup Table section.
Text: "Measured sequentially under tools/runner with the same ReleaseFast binary and the same 4x4 input artifact."
No evidence file path, no exact commands, no binary path, no input artifact path or hash. The T312 brief required a measured speedup table under tools/runner — the table exists but provenance is absent. Cannot verify that these numbers came from the claimed binary/input or that tools/runner was actually used.

DEFECT 6 (Class 2 — label dishonesty, medium confidence):
File: T312-findings.json, new_rows[0].wrong_answer_pass_rate.
Text: "0% (exhaustive: all 99,133,036 entries checked)"
This reports test COVERAGE (all entries checked for serial-vs-parallel agreement), not wrong_answer_pass_rate as defined in CLAIMS.md: "P(a wrong result also passes this claim's test)." A bug that affects serial and parallel paths identically would pass this test with 100% probability. The 0% figure is misleading — it conflates coverage with false-pass rate.

DEFECT 7 (Class 4 — suspicious claim, medium confidence):
File: parallel-fixpoint.md, Race Controls table row 4.
Text: "Serial vs parallel (4x4 exhaustive), 18 threads, 1 rep, PASS (99,133,036/99,133,036)"
This is listed as a test in src/t312_race_control.zig wired into zig build test. Running the full 4x4 fixpoint (99M states) as a unit test would require ~3.4 GB RSS and several minutes of wall time, dominating the test suite. This is implausible as a routinely-passing unit test alongside 383 others. I did not read the source file to verify — flagged as suspicious per the brief's catch-all.

=== WHAT I COULD NOT ESTABLISH ===
- Whether the exhaustive 4x4 test actually exists in src/t312_race_control.zig or was only described aspirationally (did not read the source — blind audit).
- Whether the speedup numbers are fabricated or just poorly documented (no evidence file to check).
- Whether any of the race-control tests exercise floating-point or just integer arithmetic (relevant to determinism claim across thread counts).

=== WHAT I NOTICED BUT DID NOT ACT ON ===
- The speedup curve flattens at 6 threads (3.0x) on an 18-core host — the prose attributes this to 6 performance cores, which is plausible but not verified.
- The 12-thread run (608s) is slightly faster than 18-thread (610s) — minor, consistent with parallelism overhead.
- The findings file notes mention "CLAIMS.md and tasks.json were modified in the working tree before I started — I did not touch them" — a working-tree hygiene note, not a defect.

=== CLAIM IDs TOUCHED ===
CODE.T312-PARALLEL-FIXPOINT (proposed status downgrade PROVEN→CLAIMED), GLOBAL.F2 (cited incorrectly as PROVEN), CODE.WZO2-BUILD-REPRO (cited incorrectly as PROVEN).
